question_or_symptom: Functional allocation handles, packet-visible GPU addresses, and internal code/kernarg storage can be conflated when a dispatch is admitted across the CP6 memory boundary.
observation: The dispatch request carries only client-owned queue, input/output allocation, and CP7 signal IDs plus generations and a fixture digest. Admission pins all four live resources, preserves the public CP6 slot VAs, materializes only the code-object and kernarg addresses in daemon-owned GPU-visible storage, and leaves the AQL completion_signal as HSA special handle zero. The trace recomputes packet and kernarg hashes and binds them to the ticket.
conclusion: Packet visibility is an explicit materialization and ownership contract, not an inference from a numeric allocation ID or host pointer.
decision: Validate every handle generation and fixture hash before admission, bind the two CP6 allocations to packet-visible VAs without changing their public identities, materialize only the pinned code/kernarg fields, and retain exact packet, code, kernarg, and manifest hashes in the trace.
invalidated_assumptions: A functional VA returned by allocation is automatically a packet-executable address.
The CP7 wire signal can be placed directly in the HSA AQL completion_signal field.
